```{r report-style, include=FALSE}
figure_dir <- tempfile("report-figures-")
dir.create(figure_dir)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  fig.path = file.path(figure_dir, "figure-"), dev = "png",
  fig.retina = 1, dpi = 180,
  echo = TRUE,

```

Prepare the full day of directed origin–destination (OD) counts for Divvy bike departures on **1 January 2026**. Follow one ride from the supplied CSV to a five-trip arrow in the default **00:00–03:00** Chicago-time window.

## Set up the example

Run the visible R blocks in order in an interactive R session from this example directory. The supplied CSV already contains the 1 January departures. The example interprets the departure clocks in `America/Chicago` and writes its prepared files in a new temporary directory.

`prepare.R` converts this case’s source records.
The local `scripts/prepare-input.R` assembles the OD pairs and writes the station and group tables.
`scripts/report-export.R` saves the prepared data and static maps when export is requested.

```{r setup}
library(bdynets)
source("scripts/prepare-input.R")
source("prepare.R")
source("scripts/report-export.R")
if (!exists("params", inherits = FALSE)) {
  params <- rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter("divvy-od-report.Rmd")$params
}

day <- "2026-01-01"
timezone <- "America/Chicago"
worked_ride_id <- "5004926658EA27AE"
work_dir <- tempfile("divvy-preparation-")
dir.create(work_dir)
```

The [prepared input guide](../../bdynets/inst/INPUT-FORMAT.md) describes the final drawing object. For other source data, choose the fields, time intervals and conversion rules that fit that data.

## Read the supplied data

Start with the [supplied one-day CSV](data/raw/202601-divvy-tripdata.csv). It contains 1,950 departures on 1 January 2026 and all 13 input columns in their supplied order. The setup’s `day` value is the expected date of this file. The [source manifest](data/raw/source-manifest.csv) records the file and its checksum.

Read the entire one-day CSV as text to preserve source IDs, timestamps and trailing spaces. The table shows the first row and the ride `5004926658EA27AE` traced through the rest of the report.

```{r read-raw}
raw_file <- "data/raw/202601-divvy-tripdata.csv"
raw_trips <- read_divvy_csv(raw_file)
preview_fields <- c("ride_id", "started_at", "ended_at", "start_station_id", "end_station_id")
worked_row <- match(worked_ride_id, raw_trips$ride_id)
preview_rows <- unique(c(1L, worked_row))
knitr::kable(raw_trips[preview_rows, preview_fields], row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Two original departures on 1 January 2026")
```

## Prepare the drawing input

### Clean the station names

The report and standalone preparation both use `prepare_divvy_day()`. It checks that all departures are on 1 January 2026, removes trailing ASCII spaces from the two station-name columns, and removes exact duplicate rows from the cleaned data before conversion. The table compares the original fields with the cleaned fields. The worked ride’s two station names are already clean, so all 13 source values for that ride carry over unchanged.

```{r clean-names}
prepared_day <- prepare_divvy_day(raw_trips, day = day, timezone = timezone)
daily_trips <- prepared_day$cleaned

knitr::kable(data.frame(
  source_rows = nrow(raw_trips),
  duplicate_rows_removed = prepared_day$input$provenance$duplicate_rows,
  start_names_changed = sum(raw_trips$start_station_name != daily_trips$start_station_name, na.rm = TRUE),
  end_names_changed = sum(raw_trips$end_station_name != daily_trips$end_station_name, na.rm = TRUE),
  worked_ride_started_at = daily_trips$started_at[worked_row]
), row.names = FALSE, caption = "Source rows, cleaning and the worked ride's departure clock")
```

### Prepare the station-level OD input

The same preparation call builds the station register (`nodes`) and the retained departures (`flows`). It pools the `start_lat`/`start_lng` and `end_lat`/`end_lng` pairs by `start_station_id` or `end_station_id`. Each station gets the separate medians of its valid paired latitudes and longitudes and its most frequent nonblank recorded name, with alphabetical ties. A ride enters `flows` when both station IDs join that located register. Saving the two tables and their metadata creates `station/input.rds`. It holds 1,230 retained departures across 512 stations, including rides that return to the same station.

```{r prepare-station}
prepared_dir <- file.path(work_dir, "prepared-data")
station_file <- write_divvy_station_input(
  prepared_day$input, output_dir = file.path(prepared_dir, "station"), source_file = raw_file
)
station_input <- readRDS(station_file)
station_flows <- station_input$flows
```

The counts below reconcile the original CSV with the station-level OD trips.
“Missing” means the departure has no usable station ID at the endpoint shown.
The “unmatched location” count covers trips whose endpoint IDs exist but
cannot both join to the located station register.

```{r station-record-counts}
counts <- station_input$provenance
data.frame(source_rows = counts$source_departures,
  duplicate_rows = counts$duplicate_rows,
  missing_origin_only = counts$missing_origin_only,
  missing_destination_only = counts$missing_destination_only,
  both_missing = counts$missing_both,
  unmatched_location = counts$unmatched_coordinates,
  retained_trips = counts$retained_trips)
```

In `station/input.rds`, the worked ride becomes one `flows` row. Its `origin_id` and `destination_id` join `nodes$node_id`. The origin is Michigan Ave & Madison St and the destination is Clark St & Chicago Ave. The table shows the calculated station medians. The coordinates are in EPSG:4326. The RDS records the `America/Chicago` departure instant, including its fractional seconds, with a trip count of one.

```{r station-tables}
node_fields <- c("node_id", "display_name", "longitude", "latitude")
flow_fields <- c("ride_id", "time", "origin_id", "destination_id", "flow")
worked_station_flow <- station_flows[match(worked_ride_id, station_flows$ride_id), flow_fields]
worked_station_ids <- c(worked_station_flow$origin_id, worked_station_flow$destination_id)
worked_nodes <- station_input$nodes[match(worked_station_ids, station_input$nodes$node_id), node_fields]
knitr::kable(worked_nodes, row.names = FALSE, digits = 6,
             caption = "The worked ride's origin and destination in the station register")

station_preview <- worked_station_flow
station_preview$time <- format(station_preview$time, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS3", tz = timezone)
knitr::kable(station_preview, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "The worked ride as a station departure in station/input.rds")
```

### Group the whole day within 1,500 metres

The report sets `aggregation_radius_m = 1500` to draw a less crowded map. On this day that setting gives 62 groups from 512 stations. `prepare_spatial_example()` considers stations in order of retained departures plus arrivals over the whole day, with station ID breaking ties. A station becomes a representative if it is more than 1,500 m from all previously chosen representatives. Once the representatives have been selected, each station joins the nearest one by great-circle distance. The group takes that station's ID, name, and coordinates.

`spatial-1500m/input.rds` records the grouped day and its `membership` table. The membership rows link the ride's endpoints to Columbus Dr & Randolph St (`CHI00345`) and State St & Chicago Ave (`CHI01772`). The grouped day sums trips that share a departure instant and an ordered pair of group IDs.

```{r prepare-spatial}
aggregation_radius_m <- 1500
spatial_dir <- file.path(prepared_dir, "spatial-1500m")
spatial_file <- prepare_spatial_example(
  output_dir = spatial_dir, station_file = station_file, radius_m = aggregation_radius_m
)
spatial_input <- readRDS(spatial_file)
membership <- spatial_input$provenance$spatial_aggregation$membership

worked_membership <- membership[match(worked_station_ids, membership$raw_node_id), ]
knitr::kable(worked_membership, row.names = FALSE, digits = 3,
             caption = "The representative assigned to each endpoint of the worked ride")
```

The grouped data retain trips whose endpoints now fall in the same group.
The block below shows the worked departure in the grouped table. Its time
is unchanged, and its two station IDs are now the ordered representative
IDs shown above.

```{r grouped-departure}
group_pair <- worked_membership$aggregate_node_id
grouped_departure <- subset(spatial_input$flows,
  time == worked_station_flow$time & origin_id == group_pair[1L] & destination_id == group_pair[2L],
  select = c(time, origin_id, destination_id, flow))
grouped_departure$time <- format(grouped_departure$time, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS3", tz = timezone)
knitr::kable(grouped_departure, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "The same departure instant in the grouped OD table")
```

### Prepare the map-ready OD frames

The report and `prepare.R` use the same three-hour default in `divvy_report_windows()`. For this sample, the eight windows span midnight on 1 January to midnight on 2 January in `America/Chicago`. Each window includes its start and excludes its end. Pass `window_minutes` to `divvy_report_windows()` to use another duration. The final window ends at the next local midnight.

`divvy_frame_inputs()` uses the same ordered-pair aggregation as `divvy_window_input()` and keeps a frame for every interval. Each `bdynets_od_pairs` object carries its start and end times, nodes, route counts and coordinates, within-group totals and provenance. Save the ordered list to `od-frames.rds` for reuse. The ordered list is the standard drawing input. The station and grouped `input.rds` files above remain tables for preparation. Each frame already contains the joined longitude and latitude of its directed endpoints, their counts, and its start and end times.

```{r prepare-map-input}
windows <- divvy_report_windows(day, timezone)
od_frames <- divvy_frame_inputs(spatial_input, windows)
map_input_file <- file.path(prepared_dir, "od-frames.rds")
saveRDS(od_frames, map_input_file, compress = "xz")
```

### Trace the ride to its arrow

Ride `5004926658EA27AE` belongs to the default 00:00–03:00 window because it
departs at 00:05:10.246. Match the departure clock to its window and use the
ordered representative IDs to find the arrow.

```{r worked-route}
worked_time <- worked_station_flow$time
worked_index <- which(windows$start_time <= worked_time & worked_time < windows$end_time)
worked_pairs <- od_frames[[worked_index]]
worked_route <- worked_pairs$routes[
  worked_pairs$routes$origin_id == group_pair[1L] &
    worked_pairs$routes$destination_id == group_pair[2L], ]
knitr::kable(worked_route, row.names = FALSE, digits = 6,
             caption = "The worked ride's directed group pair and map coordinates")
```

The station-level rows show how many trips in the same window have this pair of representative groups. In the default three-hour frame, the five trips contribute `flow = 5` to the arrow from `CHI00345` to `CHI01772`. Trips in the reverse direction have their own pair.

```{r worked-route-departures}
group_by_station <- setNames(membership$aggregate_node_id, membership$raw_node_id)
same_group_pair <- group_by_station[station_flows$origin_id] == group_pair[1L] &
  group_by_station[station_flows$destination_id] == group_pair[2L]
in_window <- station_flows$time >= worked_pairs$start_time & station_flows$time < worked_pairs$end_time
worked_route_departures <- station_flows[same_group_pair & in_window, flow_fields]
worked_route_departures$started_at <- daily_trips$started_at[
  match(worked_route_departures$ride_id, daily_trips$ride_id)
]
knitr::kable(
  worked_route_departures[c("ride_id", "started_at", "origin_id", "destination_id", "flow")],
  row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Departures assigned to the worked route in its window"
)
```

## Draw the selected window

Pass the complete `od-frames.rds` to `traffic_od_map()` and select a prepared window by its start time. With the default three-hour windows, 00:00 selects 00:00–03:00 in Chicago. Choose a start in the prepared series to draw another window. The package calculates the colour classes from the route counts across the entire input. Within-group trips contribute to each window’s total.

### Load the offline background

Load the supplied Chicago OpenStreetMap background prepared from OpenFreeMap vector tiles. The map focuses on the nodes drawn in the selected window. The coloured arrows use the prepared group coordinates. The full drawing input sets the trip-count colour classes.

```{r load-street-context}
street_file <- "data/basemap-cache/chicago.geojson.gz"
basemap <- if (isTRUE(params$basemap)) {
  jsonlite::read_json(street_file, simplifyVector = FALSE)
}
```

### Draw one OD window

```{r od-map, fig.width=5.1, fig.height=9.5, out.width="64%", fig.align="center", fig.cap='Divvy departures in the selected time window.'}
plot_time <- params$plot_time
traffic_od_map(
  map_input_file, time_label = plot_time, basemap = basemap,
  extent = "frame", padding = 0.10,
  title = paste("Divvy departures aggregated within", aggregation_radius_m / 1000, "km"),
  caption = "Curves show direction between representative stations."
)
```

## Export the results

Preparation saves its working files in a temporary directory. The draw calls
use the current R graphics device. When running the blocks with `Rscript` and
no device open, R can create `Rplots.pdf` in the working directory. To regenerate the report HTML and keep the selected map and complete drawing data, run this command from the example directory:

```sh
Rscript run.R 00:00 --offline --export
```

Replace `00:00` with another prepared frame start to draw that frame. The default destination is a new `output/` directory. To use a different new directory, add `--output-dir NEW_DIRECTORY`.

The command saves the selected map at `output/maps/divvy-od.png`. `output/prepared-data/od-frames.rds` contains all prepared frames and can be passed to the same plotting function to draw another frame. The `station/` and `spatial-1500m/` subdirectories hold the intermediate OD data. Each has a `source-files.csv` listing the input to that preparation step. The original trip CSV stays in `data/raw/`.

```{r export-results, include=FALSE}
if (params$export) {
  export_static_report(params$export_dir, prepared_dir, c("divvy-od.png" = "od-map"))
}
```
